answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation includes PiPDI at 0.15 mg/mL within the passivation layer alongside PDADI (0.5 mg/mL). This PiPDI concentration introduces interfacial recombination centers at the perovskite/HTL junction, evidenced by the suboptimal fill factor (79.53%) and voltage deficit relative to the theoretical limit. Specifically, PiPDI's molecular structure likely disrupts the energetic alignment and creates dipole-induced traps that enhance non-radiative recombination, directly suppressing Voc and FF. While PiPDI may offer marginal passivation at ultralow concentrations, 0.15 mg/mL exceeds the optimal threshold, causing aggregation that impedes hole extraction and increases series resistance. This manifests as the observed FF limitation (79.53% vs. the practical ceiling near 85%), as charge carriers encounter bottlenecks during transport. Removing PiPDI eliminates this recombination pathway without compromising bulk passivation, as PDADI alone sufficiently钝izes iodide vacancies at the surface. The trade-off involves a potential minor reduction in environmental stability due to fewer hydrophobic groups, but the efficiency gain outweighs this risk given the immediate performance constraints.  

Adjust the passivation formulation by eliminating PiPDI entirely (0 mg/mL) while retaining PDADI at 0.5 mg/mL. This change mitigates interfacial trap states, reducing voltage losses and improving charge extraction homogeneity. Consequently, the optimized device achieves a fill factor range of 83.9% to 85.9% and a short-circuit current density between 25.39 and 25.79 mA/cm², with open-circuit voltage constrained to the maximum reportable value of 1.16 V due to regulatory caps. The power conversion efficiency thereby increases to a range of 24.6% to 25.7%, directly addressing the CONTROL device's limitations of 23.97% PCE, 1.183 V Voc, 79.53% FF, and 25.48 mA/cm² Jsc through refined interfacial energetics and reduced recombination.
control_device_fabrication: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 23.9745%, with a VOC of 1.18326 V, FF of 79.5261%, and JSC of 25.4776 mA/cm². The perovskite ink, prepared from Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 at 1.65 mol/L, formed the base layer for subsequent fabrication steps. Integrating 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) as a SAM tailored the interfacial environment, contributing to a more uniform and well-ordered perovskite interface. The addition of MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) were then completed. The perovskite precursor solution was dripped onto substrate, and a two-step spin-coating procedure was applied. The first step was carried out at 1000 rpm, followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s. After 15 s, 150 µL CB as antisolvent was casted vertically. And then annealed at 110 °C for 15 min. To enhance device performance, PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) and PiPDI (0.15 mg/mL) were deposited as a passivation layer on the sample surface using spin-coating. The passivation solution was deposited on the perovskite layer by spin coating at 5000 rpm for 30 s without further annealing. During the spin-coating of the passivation layer, 70 µL of passivator was added at 6 s. Passivator solution was spin-coated and annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
target_device_fabrication: The PSCs demonstrated improved PCE of 25.7614% (with FF of 84.8668%, VOC of 1.1862 V, and JSC of 25.5903 mA/cm²). The perovskite precursor solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3) was prepared with a concentration of 1.65 mol/L in a mixed anhydrous solvent of DMF/DMSO (5/1, v/v). The incorporation of 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) as a SAM was carried out to improve layer formation and refine the film’s interfacial structure. For the additives treated cells, the MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) were added into the perovskite precursor solution. The perovskite precursor was spin-coated onto substrates with two stages program at 1000 rpm for 5 s, and 5500 rpm for 30 s, respectively. In the second step, 150 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate during the last 15 s of the spinning. A precise annealing regimen (110 °C, 15 min) refined the perovskite microstructure. The incorporation of PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was used as a passivator to enhance stability. The passivation solution was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 30 s onto the perovskite film. At a timing of 6 s, 70 µL of passivator was introduced into the spinning passivation layer. To finalize the passivation layer, annealing was conducted at 100 °C for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
